title: TMPlayer
description: Telegram video player for Android TV, phones, Windows, Linux and macOS. Playback starts while the file is still downloading.
tagline: Your Telegram videos, on the TV, in your hand and on your computer. Start watching before the download finishes.
longDescription: Videos shared through your own Telegram chats are awkward to watch on a television: download to a phone, copy the file across, then find somewhere to keep it. TMPlayer removes that detour. Scan a QR code with the phone that holds your Telegram account, open a chat, pick a video, and playback starts while the file continues downloading. On a phone the same app signs in by number and redraws itself as a Material 3 phone app rather than a TV grid.

The interesting part is the streaming layer. A custom Media3 DataSource maps ExoPlayer's reads onto TDLib's offset-based partial downloads, so seeking to the ninety-minute mark re-aims the download at that byte instead of grinding through everything before it. The window arithmetic lives in one pure class with the awkward cases pinned down by unit tests, because that is where a streaming player either works or does not. The project carries about 1,400 tests in all.

It also runs on a computer. The desktop app is Compose Multiplatform over the same shared core as the Android app, plays through libmpv, and ships as an MSI installer for Windows and an AppImage for Linux, with an AUR recipe for Arch. Since 1.26.0 there is a macOS preview for Apple Silicon, built, signed and self-tested on CI.

Everything is shaped by the hardware it targets, a TV stick with a gigabyte of RAM and under 5 GB of usable storage. One video is cached at a time, and Low storage mode keeps only a rolling 200 MB window of a stream on disk, so a film larger than the free space still plays. Previews come straight from Telegram, and a single universal APK covers every architecture. There is no catalogue and no server: the app talks to Telegram with your own credentials, and to the poster lookups while they are on, and nothing else.

It ships with its own site at tmplayer.org, in 21 languages, covering features, install steps for each platform, a changelog with an RSS feed, an FAQ, privacy and lawful use, so a stranger can decide whether to install it before downloading anything.
features: QR code sign-in on a TV, phone number sign-in on a phone, both with two-step verification
Instant playback and real seeking, both while the file is still downloading
MKV, MP4, AVI and TS with embedded PGS and VobSub subtitles and switchable audio tracks
Software decoding for DTS, TrueHD and E-AC3 when the device lacks the silicon
Episode filenames parsed locally, with previous, next and autoplay across a series
One video cached at a time, with continue watching positions that survive a power cut
Low storage mode, which streams a film larger than the free space
The same APK draws a D-pad TV interface or a Material 3 phone app
A desktop app for Windows, Linux and macOS, as an MSI installer, an AppImage and a DMG preview
Posters, overviews and episode names from TMDB, TVmaze and AniList, and rows on the Android TV home screen
Skip intro and credits, speed per series, preferred languages, watch later and season downloads
Backups, an app PIN and a kids lock with allowed chats

title: TapTL
description: Live on-screen translator for Android games. Reads the text on screen and draws English over it, offline.
tagline: Read your game in English. Live English over the text in your games, from any of 12 languages, with no root and nothing sent online.
longDescription: TapTL started with the Chinese release of Valorant Mobile, which has no English option. It records the screen through Android's normal screen sharing, reads the text on the phone, and draws English boxes over the original, coloured to match the background behind them. It works with any app or game that allows screen capture, and turns on and off from a Quick Settings tile.

Each frame is shrunk to a tiny grayscale copy and compared with the last one, so a still screen costs nothing and only the parts that changed get read. ML Kit does the text recognition and the translation, both on the device. A word list built from the official Valorant names is checked first, so agents, weapons and maps keep their real English names instead of a literal translation. When the whole screen keeps moving, as it does in a match, the overlay hides itself.

It needs no root, no Accessibility service and no account. The overlay cannot be touched, so every tap still reaches the game, and nothing reads game memory or injects input. After a one-time download of about 40 MB per language it works offline. The site at taptl.pages.dev has a before and after slider made from real captures on a Poco F5.
features: Twelve source languages, all translated to English
On-device text recognition and translation with ML Kit, offline after a one-time download
Only the changed parts of the screen are read, so a still screen costs no work
Built-in word list for Valorant Mobile CN with the official English names
An overlay that cannot be touched, so taps still reach the game
A Quick Settings tile to turn it on and off, with Stop in the notification
No root, no Accessibility service and no account

title: LangSync
description: Command line tool that keeps every locale file in step with one English source, translating only what changed.
tagline: Keeps every locale file in step with one source of truth, and only translates what changed.
longDescription: Keeping a dozen locale files in step with an English one by hand means missed keys and stale strings. LangSync treats one file as the source of truth. It works out which keys are new, edited or gone, translates only those, and writes them into every target locale in parallel.

Keys are grouped into batch requests rather than sent one at a time, which cut the network calls by up to 98 percent. Placeholders like {name} and inline tags are protected, and ICU plural and select messages are parsed so only the readable text is translated. Every rebuilt message is parsed again before it is written, so a translation that would break the syntax is rejected instead of shipped.

A snapshot of the source values tracks drift, so an edited English string is translated again everywhere. Orphan keys are reported, and only removed when you ask. Every error and warning ends with the exact command that fixes it.
features: Parallel sync across every locale from one source file
Batch translation, up to 98 percent fewer network calls
Placeholder and ICU plural and select protection, checked again before writing
Drift detection, so edited source strings are translated again
Nested objects and arrays translated element by element
A check mode for CI, and a fix command printed with every error

title: Resume Builder
description: Free resume builder with live preview, JSON import and export, and PDF upload that fills it in.
tagline: A free, developer-focused resume builder with live preview, JSON import/export, and AI-powered resume upload.
longDescription: Resume Builder (resumebuilder.js.org) is a free web app for building resumes with a live-editing interface. Fill in structured sections for personal information, experience, skills, education, and projects, and watch the resume render in real time. It can also ingest an existing PDF resume and convert it to an editable format, with optional AI assistance through a Gemini API key.

Resume data exports and re-imports as JSON, so a resume is a file you own, not an account you rent. Finished resumes download as PDF. Everything stays local: data lives in the browser's localStorage and never touches a server, which also means the whole app can be self-hosted as static files.
The project earned a js.org subdomain through a merged PR to the js-org registry, a small badge of honor for open-source JavaScript projects.
features: Live-editing form with real-time resume preview
PDF resume upload with optional AI conversion via Gemini
JSON import and export of resume data
One-click PDF download
Light and dark themes with sample data loading
Fully client-side, data stays in localStorage

title: Email Sender
description: Personalised bulk outreach to recruiters from your own Gmail. No third-party email service involved.
tagline: A small open-source Next.js app for sending personalized bulk job-outreach emails from your own Gmail account.
longDescription: EmailxSender helps job seekers send personalized outreach or bulk recruiter emails directly from their own Gmail account using a Gmail App Password. No third-party email service, no shady middleman. Log in with your Gmail address and app password, compose the email, attach a PDF resume, add recipients, and send. Each recipient gets an individual delivery instead of being dumped into a BCC list.

It is privacy-focused by construction: credentials live only in the browser's localStorage and are used solely to talk to Gmail's SMTP. The app auto-saves drafts, keeps a per-account send history so you can see who you already contacted, and ships dark and light themes. MIT licensed and open to contributions.
features: Bulk sending with individual per-recipient delivery, no BCC lists
Gmail App Password auth, credentials stored only in localStorage
Auto-saved drafts for subject, body, recipients, and resume
Per-Gmail send history
PDF resume attachment
Dark and light themes

title: Image Cropper
description: shadcn/ui registry image cropper with drag and drop, aspect ratios and file-size limits.
tagline: A ShadcnUI-registry React component for uploading and cropping images with drag-and-drop and configurable aspect ratios.
longDescription: Image Cropper is a reusable React image-crop component distributed through a custom ShadcnUI registry. Developers install the full source code into their project with a single CLI command (pnpm, npm, yarn, or bun all work) instead of adding another black-box dependency, which means the component is theirs to modify.

The component handles image selection via drag-and-drop or file browsing, then presents an interactive cropping interface built on react-easy-crop. It is configured through props: aspectRatio for 16:9, 1:1 and friends, fileLimitMB for upload constraints, and an onCropComplete callback that returns the cropped result.
features: Installable via a custom ShadcnUI registry, full source ownership
Drag-and-drop or file-browse image selection
Configurable aspect ratios
File-size limits via a single prop
onCropComplete callback for the cropped output
Works with pnpm, npm, yarn, and bun

title: No Secrets
description: Concept landing page for NoSecrets, a zero-sugar electrolyte drink brand. A design study, not a live store.
tagline: A concept landing page for a zero-sugar electrolyte brand, built as a design study.
longDescription: A concept design, not a live store or a commissioned site. I made it to try out a product landing page for an Indian electrolyte drink: powdered sachets in three flavours, Orange Refresh, Berry Boost and Lime Zest, with prices in rupees, under the line 'Hydration, Honestly'.

The page is built around the product's claims (zero sugar, six electrolytes, made for India) and benefit sections for energy, focus, skin, digestion, sleep and recovery. The testimonials and prices are sample content. Built with Next.js, Tailwind CSS and Framer Motion.
features: Product cards with flavours, rupee pricing and sold-out states
Benefit sections built around six electrolytes and zero sugar
Sample testimonial section
Brand story section on clean ingredients
Animated Next.js and Framer Motion landing page

title: Donut Website
description: Animated donut-shop website recreating a Glaze Co design concept with React and Framer Motion.
tagline: An animated donut-shop website recreating a Glaze Co design concept with React and Framer Motion.
longDescription: Donut Website is an animated storefront site inspired by a Glaze Co donut-shop design concept from Behance. It takes a designer's static concept and turns it into a living build, a useful exercise in translating motion design into production code.

It features scroll-driven animations, interactive transitions and hover effects, and a responsive layout for all devices. Built with React and Framer Motion, styled with Tailwind CSS, and bundled with Vite.

Responsive layout for all devices
Faithful implementation of a Behance design concept
React, Framer Motion, Tailwind CSS, and Vite

title: Trello Clone
description: Trello-style kanban board with animated drag and drop and search filters, backed by Appwrite.
tagline: A Trello 2.0-style kanban board built with Next.js, with drag-and-drop and search.
longDescription: A kanban-style task board modeled on Trello 2.0: boards, columns, and cards with animated drag-and-drop and a search bar that filters todos in place.

The frontend is Next.js with Tailwind CSS and HeadlessUI, and todos are fetched dynamically from an Appwrite backend. Built in 2023 as a deep-dive into drag-and-drop interactions and optimistic UI updates.

Animated drag-and-drop for cards
Search bar with live filtering
Appwrite-backed dynamic data
Next.js with optimized images

title: Notes App
description: Animated sticky-notes web app with draggable cards that persist locally in the browser.
tagline: An animated sticky-notes app with draggable cards that persist locally in the browser.
longDescription: A sticky-notes app where every note is a draggable card. Type into a card to create or edit a note, drag it anywhere within the container, and watch the save indicator flip between saving, saved, and needs-content states.
Notes persist in the browser's localStorage, so they survive reloads without any backend. Built with React, Tailwind CSS, and Framer Motion for the stack-based animations and drag physics.
features: Create and edit notes in draggable cards
Drag constraints within the parent container
localStorage persistence across reloads
Visual save-status feedback
Framer Motion animations

title: Drum Kit
description: A browser drum kit you play with your keyboard. Seven keys, instant percussion.
tagline: A browser drum kit you play with your keyboard. Seven keys, instant percussion.
longDescription: Drum Kit turns the keyboard into a percussion instrument: press a, s, d, f, j, k, or l and the matching drum fires instantly. The interface is deliberately minimal so nothing gets between you and the noise.
Built in 2022 with plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript as an exercise in DOM events and audio playback. No framework, no build step, just the web platform.
features: Seven keyboard-mapped drum sounds
Instant audio playback on keypress
Minimalist single-page interface
Pure HTML, CSS, and JavaScript

title: Simon Game
description: The Simon Says memory game as a web app. Repeat the growing sequence for as long as you can.
tagline: The classic Simon memory game in the browser. Press a key and repeat the growing sequence.
longDescription: A web implementation of the classic 1978 Simon electronic memory game. Press any key to start, then repeat an increasingly long sequence of color flashes and sounds until your memory gives out.
Hosted on GitHub Pages and built in 2022 with HTML, CSS, and jQuery. A zero-dependency static site that still holds up.
features: Classic Simon sequence-memory gameplay
Keyboard-triggered game start
Color and sound sequences that grow each round
Zero-dependency static site on GitHub Pages

title: Result Management System

longDescription: A full-stack student result-tracking system: view grades, class schedules, and performance insights in one place. The frontend is a Next.js app deployed on Vercel; a separate Express and Node backend persists everything in MongoDB.

title: Netflix Clone
description: A Netflix-style streaming UI powered by the TMDB API, with genre rows, a featured banner, and My List.
tagline: A Netflix-style streaming UI powered by the TMDB API, with genre rows, a featured banner, and My List.
longDescription: A recreation of the Netflix India browsing experience: a featured spotlight banner with Play and My List actions, a user avatar, and horizontal poster rows for Originals, Trending Now, Top Rated, and genres from Action to Documentaries.

All imagery and metadata come from The Movie Database (TMDB) API, so the catalog mixes Indian and international titles like Stranger Things, Squid Game, and The Shawshank Redemption. Built with Next.js and Tailwind CSS and deployed on Vercel.

Featured hero banner with Play and My List actions
Category rows for Originals, Trending, Top Rated, and five genres
Poster-grid browsing matching the Netflix visual style

Bootstrap-based responsive UI
